newsitem.title: ITALY: Bertinotti-Italy must keep 51 pct of Stet.
newsitem.headline: Bertinotti-Italy must keep 51 pct of Stet.

text.p: Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti reaffirmed in a newspaper interview on Wednesday that 51 percent of Italian telecoms company Stet should remain in public hands after its partial privatisation.
Bertinotti, whose party assures the government's parliamentary majority, also told business newspaper Il Sole-24 Ore that he was against a supplementary budget for 1997.
On Stet, expected to be privatised later this year, he said his party was in favour of "issuing a quota of shares".
"We believe that the sector must have a public leadership through which it can achieve international accords and for that reason we propose maintaining 51 percent in public hands," he said.
Bertinotti said there should be "only one budget in 1997".
"The problem is of content. (There should be) neither taxes nor cuts," he said, adding budgetary figures should take account of revenue raised from a crackdown on tax evasion.
He noted that the 1997 budget approved by parliament last month included a one-off "Euro tax" levy to help Italy meet the terms for membership of Europe's planned single currency.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi has said a supplementary budget for 1997 is a probability after the 1996 deficit overshot its official target. He also has proposed bringing forward passage of the 1998 budget forward by four months to mid-August.
